title: Perf bench scratch - latency/throughput notes
content:
Goal: quick reproducible runs to investigate unusually high p95 tail latency for long-context workloads (>=4k tokens). Run small matrix to see impact of batching, KV cache, and quantization profile.

Environment:
- Node: dev-gpu-03 (p4d.24xlarge, A100 40GB VMs)
- Runtime build: serving-runtime@main (commit a1b2c3d) with latest kv-cache changes (WIP)
- Model: Llama-2-7B-chat (q4_0 quantized build used by default)
- Inference server flags: --prefetch-kv=true --max-batch-delay-ms=12 --enable-cont-batching=true
- Client: bench/bench_client.py (simple parallel worker harness)

Commands used (local bench harness):
- python bench/bench_client.py --host dev-gpu-03:443 --model llama2-7b-q4_0 --batch-sizes 1,4,8 --seq-lens 512,2048,8192 --kv-cache on,off --iters 200
- single-request debug: curl -X POST https://dev-gpu-03/api/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":512}'

Raw results (aggregated, averages over 200 iters):
Run | batch | seq_len | kv_cache | p50_latency_ms | p95_latency_ms | throughput_tok_s
----+-------+--------+---------+---------------+---------------+----------------
 1  |   1   |  512   |  off    |     11.8      |     32.4      |    840
 2  |   4   |  512   |  off    |     18.3      |     58.9      |   3100
 3  |   1   | 2048   |  off    |     46.1      |    180.2      |    720
 4  |   1   | 2048   |  on     |     29.7      |     92.5      |   1100
 5  |   4   | 2048   |  on     |     45.2      |    140.8      |   3800
 6  |   1   | 8192   |  off    |    210.5      |   1250.1      |    260
 7  |   1   | 8192   |  on     |    124.9      |    520.6      |    480
 8  |   4   | 8192   |  on     |    145.0      |    870.4      |   1600

Quick observations:
- KV cache ON significantly reduces p50/p95 for long context runs (2048/8192). p95 improvement roughly 2-3x in these runs.
- Batching increases throughput as expected, but p95 suffers at large seq_len when kv-cache is OFF (see run 6 vs 3).
- For 8192 tokens, we still see heavy tail events (p95 >> p50) even with KV cache; suspected causes: occasional kernel fallbacks + GC pauses in runtime when sequence windows cross alignment boundaries.
- Throughput (tokens/s) scales roughly linearly with batch until GPU memory/kerneI contention; q4_0 seems stable for these sizes.

Immediate hypotheses to test next:
- There are occasional spikes when model switches kernel path for attention (e.g., fallback to non-fused attention). Need profiler traces to confirm.
- Networking: a small number of runs had client-side retries (I saw 500s in logs) \u2014 correlate with p95 spikes.
- GC / allocator fragmentation when KV cache grows beyond X MB \u2014 check allocator metrics.

Next steps / action items:
- [ ] Run same matrix with --enable-kernel-logging and capture server logs for p95 windows (target runs 3,6,7). (Assign to: Maya)
- [ ] Add tracing (span per request) to correlate client latency with server internal spans. (Assign to: me)
- [ ] Re-run with int8 (q5_x) profile to confirm quantization interaction with kernel selection. (Assign to: Ethan)
- [ ] Add a low-overhead periodic heap/allocator snapshot during long seq runs to detect fragmentation. (Assign to: eng-sre)

Notes / misc:
- I saw one anomalous run where p95 jumped to ~2.8s for a 2048 run with KV ON; server log had a CUDA error that auto-recovered (logged but not bubbled). Need to capture full stderr from that time window.
- Useful quick filter to extract suspect windows from logs: grep 'latency=.*p95' server.log | awk '$NF > 500'

Scratch ideas:
- Could we pre-warm the fused-attn kernels for predicted long-context requests? Maybe pre-touch memory for KV to avoid page faults.
- Evaluate a per-model config that lowers max-batch-delay-ms for >4k contexts to reduce head-of-line.

References:
- quick perf script: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-tools/blob/main/bench/bench_client.py
- previous notes: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/456-perf-notes

Timestamped dumps saved to: s3://redwood-inference-dev/perf-dumps/jordan-2026-03-07/ (contains traces and server logs for runs 3,6,7)

Unresolved questions:
- Are we seeing kernel fallback due to sequence-length alignment? Need kernel debug prints to be sure.
- How many customer requests hit >4k on prod (quick ask to analytics) \u2014 if low, deprioritize heavy fixes.

End of scratch log.
